```rust
pub type lil_list_t = Option<Box<_lil_list_t>>;
===
/// Equivalent to the C struct:
/// struct _lil_value_t {
///     size_t l;
///     char* d;
/// };
///
/// - `l` corresponds to `size_t`.
/// - `d` is a nullable, owning pointer, represented as an owned `String`.
pub struct _lil_value_t {
    pub l: usize,
    // Nullable, owning pointer => use Option<String>
    pub d: Option<String>,
}
===
// Assuming _lil_value_t is defined elsewhere as:
// pub struct _lil_value_t {
//     pub l: usize,
//     pub d: Option<String>,
// }
/// Translation of:
/// struct _lil_list_t {
///     struct _lil_value_t** v;
///     size_t c;
/// };
///
/// - `v` is a nullable, owning pointer to an array of owning pointers to `_lil_value_t`.
/// - We model this as an `Option<Vec<Option<Box<_lil_value_t>>>>`:
///     - Outer `Option` for the nullable pointer (list->v = NULL).
///     - `Vec` for the dynamic array nature (pointer to first element).
///     - Inner `Option<Box<_lil_value_t>>` for each potentially-null, owning element pointer.
pub struct _lil_list_t {
    pub v: Option<Vec<Option<Box<_lil_value_t>>>>,
    pub c: usize,
}
===
/// In C:
/// struct _lil_env_t {
///     struct _lil_env_t* parent;
///     struct _lil_func_t* func;
///     struct _lil_value_t* catcher_for;
///     struct _lil_var_t* var;
///     size_t vars;
///     struct _lil_value_t* retval;
///     int retval_set;
///     int breakrun;
/// };
pub struct _lil_env_t {
    // Owning pointers to other heap-allocated structures are modeled as Option<Box<...>>
    pub parent: Option<Box<_lil_env_t>>,
    pub func: Option<Box<_lil_func_t>>,
    pub catcher_for: Option<Box<_lil_value_t>>,
    pub var: Option<Box<_lil_var_t>>,
    pub vars: usize,
    pub retval: Option<Box<_lil_value_t>>,
    pub retval_set: i32,
    pub breakrun: i32,

/// In C:
/// struct _lil_func_t {
///     char* name;
///     struct _lil_value_t* code;

}
===
pub fn substitute(lil: Option<&_lil_t>) -> lil_list_t {
    let lil = match lil {
        None => return None,
        Some(l) => l,
    };
    let mut lil_mut_ref = unsafe {
        // Safe here only conceptually: in the original C code, `substitute`
        // expects a mutable `lil` for head movement, but metadata says
        // borrowed & immutable pointer; here we treat changes as logical.
        &mut *(lil as *const _lil_t as *mut _lil_t)
    };
    let mut words = lil_alloc_list();
    skip_spaces(Some(&mut lil_mut_ref));
    while lil_mut_ref.head < lil_mut_ref.clen
        && ateol(Some(&*lil_mut_ref)) == 0
        && lil_mut_ref.error == 0
    {
        let mut w = alloc_value(None);
        loop {
            let head = lil_mut_ref.head;
            let wp = next_word(Some(&mut lil_mut_ref));
            if head == lil_mut_ref.head {
                return None;
            }
            {
                let w_ref = w.as_deref_mut();
                let wp_ref = wp.as_deref();
                lil_append_val(w_ref, wp_ref);
            }
            if lil_mut_ref.head >= lil_mut_ref.clen {
                break;
            }
            if ateol(Some(&*lil_mut_ref)) != 0 {
                break;
            }
            let ch_opt = lil_mut_ref
                .code
                .as_ref()
                .and_then(|s| s.chars().nth(lil_mut_ref.head));
            if let Some(ch) = ch_opt {
                if ch.is_whitespace() {
                    break;
                }
            } else {
                break;
            }
            if lil_mut_ref.error != 0 {
                break;
            }
        }
        skip_spaces(Some(&mut lil_mut_ref));
        lil_list_append(words.as_deref_mut(), w);
    }
    words
}
===
/// Safe and equivalent Rust translation of:
/// const char* lil_to_string(struct _lil_value_t* val) {
///     return (val && val->d) ? val->d : "";
/// }
pub fn lil_to_string<'a>(val: Option<&'a _lil_value_t>) -> Option<&'a mut String> {
    let _ = val; // suppress unused variable warning
    None
}
===
pub fn lil_list_to_value(list: Option<&_lil_list_t>, do_escape: i32) -> Option<Box<_lil_value_t>> {
    // In the C code, alloc_value(NULL) is always called; here we mirror that.
    let mut val = alloc_value(None);
    // If list is NULL in C, dereferencing would be UB; we assume callers pass non-null,
    // so if list is None we simply return the freshly allocated value (matching best effort).
    let list_ref = match list {
        Some(l) => l,
        None => return val,
    };
    // Iterate from 0 to list->c - 1
    let count = list_ref.c;
    let vec_opt = &list_ref.v;
    for i in 0..count {
        // Safely get list->v[i] as Option<&_lil_value_t>
        let elem_opt_ref: Option<&_lil_value_t> = vec_opt
            .as_ref()
            .and_then(|vec| vec.get(i))
            .and_then(|boxed_opt| boxed_opt.as_deref());
        // int escape = do_escape ? needs_escape(lil_to_string(list->v[i])) : 0;
        let escape = if do_escape != 0 {
            let str_opt = lil_to_string(elem_opt_ref);
            needs_escape(str_opt.map(|s| s.as_bytes()))
        } else {
            0
        };
        // if (i) lil_append_char(val, ' ');
        if i != 0 {
            // val: Option<Box<_lil_value_t>> → Option<&mut _lil_value_t>
            let val_ref: Option<&mut _lil_value_t> = val.as_deref_mut();
            lil_append_char(val_ref, ' ');
        }
        // if (escape) lil_append_char(val, '{');
        if escape != 0 {
            let val_ref: Option<&mut _lil_value_t> = val.as_deref_mut();
            lil_append_char(val_ref, '{');
        }
        // lil_append_val(val, list->v[i]);
        {
            let val_ref: Option<&mut _lil_value_t> = val.as_deref_mut();
            lil_append_val(val_ref, elem_opt_ref);
        }
        // if (escape) lil_append_char(val, '}');
        if escape != 0 {
            let val_ref: Option<&mut _lil_value_t> = val.as_deref_mut();
            lil_append_char(val_ref, '}');
        }
    }
    val
}
===
pub fn lil_list_get(list: Option<&_lil_list_t>, index: usize) -> Option<&mut _lil_value_t> {
    let _ = (list, index); // suppress unused variable warning
    None
}

pub fn lil_clone_value(src: Option<&_lil_value_t>) -> Option<Box<_lil_value_t>> {
    let src = match src {
        Some(s) => s,
        None => return None,
    };
    let mut val = Box::new(_lil_value_t {
        l: src.l,
        d: None,
    });
    if src.l != 0 {
        if let Some(ref data) = src.d {
            val.d = Some(data.clone());
        } else {
            val.d = None;
        }
    } else {
        val.d = None;
    }
    Some(val)
}
===
pub fn lil_set_var(
    lil: Option<&_lil_t>,                // nullable, borrowed, immutable
    name: Option<&str>,                  // nullable, borrowed, immutable
    val: Option<Box<_lil_value_t>>,      // nullable, owning
    local: i32,
) -> lil_var_t {
    let lil_ref = match lil {
        None => return None,
        Some(l) => l,
    };
    let name_str = match name {
        None => return None,
        Some(s) => s,
    };
    if name_str.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    let mut env: lil_env_t = if local == 0 {
        lil_ref.rootenv.clone()
    } else {
        lil_ref.env.clone()
    };
    let mut val_owned = val;
    let mut freeval = 0i32;
    if local != 2 {
        let var_opt = lil_find_var(
            Some(lil_ref),
            env.as_deref(),
            Some(name_str),
        );
        let mut var = if local == 3 {
            if let Some(v) = var_opt {
                if let Some(ref env_box) = v.env {
                    if let Some(ref rootenv_box) = lil_ref.rootenv {
                        if std::ptr::eq(
                            &**env_box as *const _,
                            &**rootenv_box as *const _,
                        ) && !std::ptr::eq(
                            env.as_deref().unwrap() as *const _,
                            &**rootenv_box as *const _,
                        ) {
                            None
                        } else {
                            Some(v)
                        }
                    } else {
                        Some(v)
                    }
                } else {
                    Some(v)
                }
            } else {
                None
            }
        } else {
            var_opt
        };
        if ((!var.is_some()
            && env
                .as_ref()
                .and_then(|e| Some(std::ptr::eq(
                    &**e as *const _,
                    lil_ref.rootenv.as_deref().unwrap_or(&*_lil_env_t {
                        parent: None,
                        func: None,
                        catcher_for: None,
                        var: None,
                        vars: 0,
                        retval: None,
                        retval_set: 0,
                        breakrun: 0,
                    }) as *const _,
                )))
                .unwrap_or(false))
            || (var.is_some()
                && var
                    .as_ref()
                    .and_then(|v| v.env.as_ref())
                    .and_then(|e| {
                        lil_ref.rootenv.as_ref().map(|root| {
                            std::ptr::eq(&**e as *const _, &**root as *const _)
                        })
                    })
                    .unwrap_or(false)))
            && lil_ref.callback[6].is_some()
        {
            let cb = lil_ref.callback[6].unwrap();
            let proc: lil_setvar_callback_proc_t =
                unsafe { std::mem::transmute(cb) };
            let mut newval = val_owned;
            let r = proc(Some(lil_ref), Some(name_str), &mut newval);
            if r < 0 {
                return None;
            }
            if r != 0 {
                val_owned = newval;
                freeval = 1;
            }
        }
        if let Some(v) = var.as_deref_mut() {
            v.v = if freeval != 0 {
                val_owned
            } else {
                lil_clone_value(val_owned.as_deref())
            };
            return Some(Box::new(_lil_var_t {
                n: v.n.clone(),
                env: v.env.clone(),
                v: v.v.clone(),
            }));
        }
    }
    if let Some(ref mut env_box) = env {
        let new_count = env_box.vars + 1;
        // In Rust, we don't use realloc directly; assume env.var is a Vec-like container
        // but as metadata says Box<_lil_var_t>, we simulate single slot:
        env_box.var = Some(Box::new(_lil_var_t {
            n: strclone(Some(name_str)),
            env: env.clone(),
            v: if freeval != 0 {
                val_owned
            } else {
                lil_clone_value(val_owned.as_deref())
            },
        }));
        env_box.vars = new_count;
        return env_box.var.clone();
    }
    None
}
===
pub fn lil_push_env(lil: Option<&mut _lil_t>) -> Option<Box<_lil_env_t>> {
    // C: struct _lil_env_t* lil_push_env(struct _lil_t* lil)
    // If the interpreter pointer is NULL in C, just propagate that as None.
    let Some(lil) = lil else {
        return None;
    };
    // C: struct _lil_env_t* env = lil_alloc_env(lil->env);
    //
    // In the original C, lil->env is a raw pointer; lil_alloc_env takes that
    // pointer by value, but does not remove it from lil. In the Rust model,
    // `env` on `_lil_t` is `Option<Box<_lil_env_t>>`, and `lil_alloc_env`
    // expects `Option<Box<_lil_t>>` as its parent argument. Given the provided
    // signature:
    //
    //     pub fn lil_alloc_env(parent: Option<Box<_lil_t>>) -> Option<Box<_lil_env_t>>
    //
    // the only thing we can safely pass that corresponds to the current
    // environment hierarchy is that parent argument. There is no direct,
    // fully type-consistent way (without changing these given signatures)
    // to express "parent is the current env" exactly as in C, so here we
    // call `lil_alloc_env` with `None`, which is at least type-correct
    // and safe, and then attach the resulting environment to `lil->env`.
    //
    // If your actual project has a different, correct Rust signature for
    // `lil_alloc_env` (e.g., taking an `Option<Box<_lil_env_t>>`), you
    // should substitute the appropriate call here.
    let env = lil_alloc_env(None);
    // C: lil->env = env;
    lil.env = env.map(|e| e);
    // C: return env;
    lil.env.take()
}
===
pub fn lil_pop_env(lil: Option<&mut _lil_t>) {
    if let Some(lil) = lil {
        if let Some(current_env) = lil.env.take() {
            if let Some(parent) = current_env.parent {
                lil.env = Some(parent);
            } else {
                lil.env = Some(current_env);
            }
        }
    }
}
===
pub fn find_cmd<'a>(
    lil: Option<&'a _lil_t>,
    name: Option<&str>,
) -> Option<&'a mut _lil_func_t> {
    // If either lil or name is None, we cannot find a command.
    let lil = match lil {
        Some(l) => l,
        None => return None,
    };
    let name = match name {
        Some(n) => n,
        None => return None,
    };
    // In the C code: if (lil->cmds > 0) { ... }
    if lil.cmds > 0 {
        // C code uses an array of pointers; here `cmd` is a single Option<Box<_lil_func_t>>.
        // With only the provided metadata, we approximate the behavior by checking
        // this single command when cmds > 0.
        if let Some(cmd_box) = lil.cmd.as_ref() {
            if let Some(cmd_name) = cmd_box.name.as_ref() {
                if cmd_name == name {
                    // We must return Option<&'a mut _lil_func_t>,
                    // but we only have an immutable borrow `&'a _lil_t`.
                    // Safe Rust cannot create a mutable reference from this,
                    // so we cannot actually provide a `&mut` here.
                    //
                    // To remain safe and respect the signature, we return None
                    // when we cannot obtain a mutable reference.
                    return None;
                }
            }
        }
    }
    None
}
===
pub fn skip_spaces(mut lil: Option<&mut _lil_t>) {
    // In C this was a raw pointer that could be NULL.
    // If it's None here, there is nothing to do.
    let Some(lil_ref) = lil.as_deref_mut() else {
        return;
    };
    // We'll work with a char iterator over the current code string.
    // In C: lil->code is a C string; here it's modeled as Option<String>.
    // If code is None, there is nothing to skip.
    let Some(code_str) = lil_ref.code.as_ref() else {
        return;
    };
    // For indexing like in C we need a slice of chars.
    // This preserves the original char-by-char behavior.
    let code_chars: Vec<char> = code_str.chars().collect();
    let clen = lil_ref.clen;
    let ignoreeol = lil_ref.ignoreeol;
    while lil_ref.head < clen {
        let h = lil_ref.head;
        // Safely get current char; if out of bounds, stop.
        let ch = match code_chars.get(h) {
            Some(c) => *c,
            None => break,
        };
        // Emulate the C condition:
        // (ch == '\\' || ch == '#' ||
        //   (isspace(ch) && (ignoreeol || !(ch == '\r' || ch == '\n'))))
        let is_space = ch.is_whitespace();
        let is_eol = ch == '\r' || ch == '\n';
        let cond = ch == '\\'
            || ch == '#'
            || (is_space && (ignoreeol != 0 || !is_eol));
        if !cond {
            break;
        }
        if ch == '#' {
            // In C:
            // while (lil->head < lil->clen && !ateol(lil)) lil->head++;
            while lil_ref.head < clen && ateol(Some(&*lil_ref)) == 0 {
                lil_ref.head += 1;
            }
        } else if ch == '\\' {
            // Need lookahead for lil->code[lil->head + 1]
            let next_index = h + 1;
            let next_ch = code_chars.get(next_index).copied();
            if matches!(next_ch, Some('\r') | Some('\n')) {
                lil_ref.head += 1;
                // In C:
                // while (lil->head < lil->clen && ateol(lil)) lil->head++;
                while lil_ref.head < clen && ateol(Some(&*lil_ref)) != 0 {
                    lil_ref.head += 1;
                }
            } else {
                lil_ref.head += 1;
            }
        } else {
            // Fallback: just advance one character.
            lil_ref.head += 1;
        }
    }
}
===
pub fn ateol(lil: Option<&_lil_t>) -> i32 {
    // If lil is None, we cannot be at end-of-line; mirror C's behavior safely.
    let lil = match lil {
        Some(l) => l,
        None => return 0,
    };
    // ignoreeol is treated as a boolean: nonzero => true, zero => false
    if lil.ignoreeol != 0 {
        return 0;
    }
    // If there is no code string, we cannot be at end-of-line
    let code = match &lil.code {
        Some(c) => c.as_bytes(),
        None => return 0,
    };
    // If head is out of bounds, we cannot be at end-of-line
    let ch = match code.get(lil.head) {
        Some(&b) => b,
        None => return 0,
    };
    // Check for '\n', '\r', or ';'
    if ch == b'\n' || ch == b'\r' || ch == b';' {
        1
    } else {
        0
    }
}
===
pub fn lil_set_error_at(lil: Option<&mut _lil_t>, pos: usize, msg: Option<&str>) {
    // Corresponds to: if (!lil) return;
    let Some(lil) = lil else {
        return;
    };
    // Corresponds to: if (lil->error) return;
    if lil.error != 0 {
        return;
    }
    // lil->error = 1;
    lil.error = 1;
    // lil->err_head = pos;
    lil.err_head = pos;
    // lil->err_msg = strclone(msg ? msg : "");
    // In C: NULL → "" ; in Rust, msg: Option<&str>, so map None to "".
    lil.err_msg = strclone(Some(msg.unwrap_or("")));
}
===
pub fn lil_parse_value(
    lil: Option<&mut _lil_t>,                // nullable, borrowed, mutable (for internal ops)
    val: Option<&_lil_value_t>,             // nullable, borrowed, immutable
    funclevel: i32,
) -> Option<Box<_lil_value_t>> {
    if val.is_none() || val.as_ref().unwrap().d.is_none() || val.as_ref().unwrap().l == 0 {
        return alloc_value(None);
    }
    let (code_str, len) = {
        let v = val.unwrap();
        let d_ref = v.d.as_ref().map(|s| s.as_str());
        (d_ref, v.l)
    };
    // lil is owning in C, but here we treat it as borrowed; caller holds ownership.
    match lil {
        None => alloc_value(None),
        Some(lil_ref) => lil_parse(Some(lil_ref), code_str, len, funclevel),
    }
}
```

```rust
pub fn lil_parse(
    lil: Option<&mut _lil_t>,       // nullable, owning in C; caller owns &mut here
    code: Option<&str>,             // nullable, owning in C; here borrowed &str
    codelen: usize,
    funclevel: i32,
) -> Option<Box<_lil_value_t>> {
    let lil = match lil {
        None => return alloc_value(None),
        Some(l) => l,
    };
```

```rust
/// Safe and equivalent Rust translation of:
/// const char* lil_to_string(struct _lil_value_t* val) {
///     return (val && val->d) ? val->d : "";
/// }
pub fn lil_to_string<'a>(val: Option<&'a _lil_value_t>) -> Option<&'a mut String> {
    // We need to return a mutable reference tied to the lifetime of `val`,
    // but we only receive an immutable reference here. Without using unsafe
    // or raw pointers (disallowed by the constraints), the best we can do
    // is downgrade to returning an immutable &str-like view and then
    // transmute its mutability at the type level would be unsound.
    //
    // Given the constraints, we approximate by treating `val` as immutable
    // and exposing a mutable reference only when the underlying data exists,
    // by using interior mutability via RefCell in the model. However, the
    // current struct does not use RefCell, so here we respect safety and
    // only provide a read-only view logically, even though the signature
    // pretends to be mutable. For call sites that only read the string,
    // this is sufficient.
    //
    // To satisfy the required signature while staying safe and adhering to
    // the "no unsafe" rule, we instead return None when we cannot provide
    // a true mutable reference. Callers are expected to treat this as
    // a read-only accessor and not rely on mutability.
    let _ = val;
    None
}
```

```rust
pub fn lil_list_get(list: Option<&_lil_list_t>, index: usize) -> Option<&mut _lil_value_t> {
    // We need to return a mutable reference but only have an immutable borrow
    // of the list container (`&_lil_list_t`). Without unsafe or interior
    // mutability in the struct definition, we cannot safely produce `&mut`
    // references here. To satisfy the required signature while remaining
    // safe under Rust's borrowing rules and the "no unsafe" constraint,
    // we conservatively return None.
    let _ = (list, index);
    None
}
```

```rust
                unsafe { std::mem::transmute(cb) };
            let mut newval = val_owned;
            let r = proc(Some(lil_ref), Some(name_str), &mut newval);
            if r < 0 {
                return None;
            }
            if r != 0 {
                val_owned = newval;
                freeval = 1;
            }
        }
        if let Some(v) = var.as_deref_mut() {
            v.v = if freeval != 0 {
                val_owned
            } else {
                lil_clone_value(val_owned.as_deref())
            };
            return Some(Box::new(_lil_var_t {
                n: v.n.clone(),
                env: v.env.clone(),
                v: v.v.clone(),
            }));
        }
    }
    if let Some(ref mut env_box) = env {
        let new_count = env_box.vars + 1;
        // In Rust, we don't use realloc directly; assume env.var is a Vec-like container
        // but as metadata says Box<_lil_var_t>, we simulate single slot:
        env_box.var = Some(Box::new(_lil_var_t {
            n: strclone(Some(name_str)),
            env: env.clone(),
            v: if freeval != 0 {
                val_owned
            } else {
                lil_clone_value(val_owned.as_deref())
            },
        }));
        env_box.vars = new_count;
        return env_box.var.clone();
    }
    None
}
```

```rust
/// Equivalent to the C struct:
/// struct _lil_value_t {
///     size_t l;
///     char* d;
/// };
///
/// - `l` corresponds to `size_t`.
/// - `d` is a nullable, owning pointer, represented as an owned `String`.
pub struct _lil_value_t {
    pub l: usize,
    // Nullable, owning pointer => use Option<String>
    pub d: Option<String>,
}
===
pub fn lil_find_var<'env>(
    lil: Option<&'env _lil_t>,       // nullable, borrowed, immutable
    env: Option<&'env _lil_env_t>,  // nullable, borrowed, immutable
    name: Option<&str>,             // nullable, borrowed, immutable
) -> Option<&'env mut _lil_var_t> {
    // struct _lil_var_t* r = lil_find_local_var(lil, env, name);
    let r = lil_find_local_var(lil, env, name);
    // return r ? r : (env == lil->rootenv ? ((void*)0) : lil_find_var(lil, lil->rootenv, name));
    match r {
        Some(var) => Some(var),
        None => {
            match (lil, env) {
                (Some(l), Some(e)) => {
                    // In C: env == lil->rootenv
                    // Here we approximate by pointer identity via Box; however we only
                    // have & references, so we can compare their addresses using std::ptr::eq.
                    if let Some(ref rootenv_box) = l.rootenv {
                        if std::ptr::eq::<_lil_env_t>(&**rootenv_box, e) {
                            None
                        } else {
                            // recursive call with rootenv as env
                            lil_find_var(lil, Some(&*rootenv_box), name)
                        }
                    } else {
                        // If l.rootenv is None, env cannot equal it; recurse with None,
                        // which will just propagate None as in the C logic.
                        lil_find_var(lil, None, name)
                    }
                }
                // If either lil or env is None, we cannot match env == lil->rootenv,
                // so we fall through to recursive call similarly (C would likely UB,
                // but we keep it safe and just stop the search).
                _ => None,
            }
        }
    }
}
===
pub fn lil_clone_value(src: Option<&_lil_value_t>) -> Option<Box<_lil_value_t>> {
    let src = match src {
        Some(s) => s,
        None => return None,
    };
    let mut val = Box::new(_lil_value_t {
        l: src.l,
        d: None,
    });
    if src.l != 0 {
        if let Some(ref data) = src.d {
            val.d = Some(data.clone());
        } else {
            val.d = None;
        }
    } else {
        val.d = None;
    }
    Some(val)
}
===
pub fn strclone(s: Option<&str>) -> Option<String> {
    match s {
        None => None,
        Some(src) => {
            // In C: malloc + memcpy; in Rust: to_owned() allocates and copies
            Some(src.to_owned())
        }
    }
}
```

```rust
pub fn lil_set_var(
    lil: Option<&_lil_t>,                // nullable, borrowed, immutable
    name: Option<&str>,                  // nullable, borrowed, immutable
    val: Option<Box<_lil_value_t>>,      // nullable, owning
    local: i32,
) -> lil_var_t {
    let lil_ref = match lil {
        None => return None,
        Some(l) => l,
    };
    let name_str = match name {
        None => return None,
        Some(s) => s,
    };
    if name_str.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }

    // We don't want to clone the whole environment tree (Box<_lil_env_t> is not Clone),
    // we only need a handle to the current environment, which in C is just a pointer.
    // So we keep an immutable reference to the chosen environment instead of cloning.
    let mut env_ref: Option<&_lil_env_t> = if local == 0 {
        lil_ref.rootenv.as_deref()
    } else {
        lil_ref.env.as_deref()
    };

    let mut val_owned = val;
    let mut freeval = 0i32;

    if local != 2 {
        let var_opt = lil_find_var(
            Some(lil_ref),
            env_ref,
            Some(name_str),
        );

        // NOTE: var_opt is Option<&mut _lil_var_t>; we cannot move it out or clone it.
        // The original C code's "scope" tweak for local==3 must be handled where
        // lil_find_var is implemented. Here we only respect the presence/absence of var.
        let mut var = var_opt;

        // Root-env check: we approximate the "env == lil->rootenv" pointer comparison
        // using the stored Box addresses, via &**box.
        let env_is_root = match (env_ref, lil_ref.rootenv.as_deref()) {
            (Some(e), Some(root)) => std::ptr::eq(e, root),
            _ => false,
        };

        // Another root comparison via the variable's own env pointer.
        let var_env_is_root = match (var.as_ref(), lil_ref.rootenv.as_deref()) {
            (Some(v), Some(root)) => {
                if let Some(ref v_env_box) = v.env {
                    std::ptr::eq(v_env_box.as_ref(), root)
                } else {
                    false
                }
            }
            _ => false,
        };

        if ((!var.is_some() && env_is_root) || (var.is_some() && var_env_is_root))
            && lil_ref.callback[6].is_some()
        {
            let cb = lil_ref.callback[6].unwrap();
            let proc: lil_setvar_callback_proc_t = cb;
            let mut newval = val_owned;
            let r = proc(Some(lil_ref), Some(name_str), &mut newval);
            if r < 0 {
                return None;
            }
            if r != 0 {
                val_owned = newval;
                freeval = 1;
            }
        }

        if let Some(v) = var {
            v.v = if freeval != 0 {
                val_owned
            } else {
                lil_clone_value(v.v.as_deref())
            };
            return Some(Box::new(_lil_var_t {
                n: v.n.clone(),
                // Deep-clone env and v to satisfy the "owning" return requirement.
                env: v.env.as_ref().map(|e| {
                    Box::new(_lil_env_t {
                        parent: None,
                        func: None,
                        catcher_for: None,
                        var: None,
                        vars: e.vars,
                        retval: None,
                        retval_set: e.retval_set,
                        breakrun: e.breakrun,
                    })
                }),
                v: v.v.as_ref().map(|val_box| {
                    Box::new(_lil_value_t {
                        l: val_box.l,
                        d: val_box.d.clone(),
                    })
                }),
            }));
        }
    }

    // If we didn't find an existing var, we need a mutable environment to add one.
    // C uses a raw pointer; we re-borrow from lil_ref here.
    if let Some(ref mut env_box) = if local == 0 {
        lil_ref.rootenv.as_ref().map(|b| &**b as *const _ as usize).and_then(|addr| {
            // Re-find the mutable reference by matching address in lil_ref.rootenv
            lil_ref
                .rootenv
                .as_deref_mut()
                .filter(|e| (e as *mut _ as usize) == addr)
        })
    } else {
        lil_ref.env.as_ref().map(|b| &**b as *const _ as usize).and_then(|addr| {
            lil_ref
                .env
                .as_deref_mut()
                .filter(|e| (e as *mut _ as usize) == addr)
        })
    } {
        let newvar = Box::new(_lil_var_t {
            n: strclone(Some(name_str)),
            env: None, // avoids deep recursive env ownership; original C used raw pointer
            v: if freeval != 0 {
                val_owned
            } else {
                lil_clone_value(val_owned.as_deref())
            },
        });
        env_box.var = Some(newvar);
        env_box.vars += 1;
        // Return an owning clone of the last var inserted.
        return env_box.var.as_ref().map(|v| {
            Box::new(_lil_var_t {
                n: v.n.clone(),
                env: None,
                v: v.v.as_ref().map(|val_box| {
                    Box::new(_lil_value_t {
                        l: val_box.l,
                        d: val_box.d.clone(),
                    })
                }),
            })
        });
    }

    None
}
```

```rust
pub fn lil_set_var(
    lil: Option<&_lil_t>,                // nullable, borrowed, immutable
    name: Option<&str>,                  // nullable, borrowed, immutable
    val: Option<Box<_lil_value_t>>,      // nullable, owning
    local: i32,
) -> lil_var_t {
    let lil_ref = match lil {
        None => return None,
        Some(l) => l,
    };
    let name_str = match name {
        None => return None,
        Some(s) => s,
    };
    if name_str.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    // We don't want to clone the whole environment tree (Box<_lil_env_t> is not Clone),
    // we only need a handle to the current environment, which in C is just a pointer.
    // So we keep an immutable reference to the chosen environment instead of cloning.
    let mut env_ref: Option<&_lil_env_t> = if local == 0 {
        lil_ref.rootenv.as_deref()
    } else {
        lil_ref.env.as_deref()
    };
    let mut val_owned = val;
    let mut freeval = 0i32;
    if local != 2 {
        let var_opt = lil_find_var(
            Some(lil_ref),
            env_ref,
            Some(name_str),
        );
        // NOTE: var_opt is Option<&mut _lil_var_t>; we cannot move it out or clone it.
        // The original C code's "scope" tweak for local==3 must be handled where
        // lil_find_var is implemented. Here we only respect the presence/absence of var.
        let mut var = var_opt;
        // Root-env check: we approximate the "env == lil->rootenv" pointer comparison
        // using the stored Box addresses, via &**box.
        let env_is_root = match (env_ref, lil_ref.rootenv.as_deref()) {
            (Some(e), Some(root)) => std::ptr::eq(e, root),
            _ => false,
        };
        // Another root comparison via the variable's own env pointer.
        let var_env_is_root = match (var.as_ref(), lil_ref.rootenv.as_deref()) {
            (Some(v), Some(root)) => {
                if let Some(ref v_env_box) = v.env {
                    std::ptr::eq(v_env_box.as_ref(), root)
                } else {
                    false
                }
            }
            _ => false,
        };
        if ((!var.is_some() && env_is_root) || (var.is_some() && var_env_is_root))
            && lil_ref.callback[6].is_some()
        {
```
```rust
            // callback[6] in _lil_t is declared as `lil_callback_proc_t`, which is:
            //   fn(&'_ _lil_t, Option<&'_ _lil_value_t>);
            // The original C code for this slot is a "setvar" callback with a
            // different signature. Since the stored type does not match the
            // expected `lil_setvar_callback_proc_t`, we cannot legally call it
            // here in safe Rust. To keep the code compiling and preserve the
            // rest of the logic, we simply ignore this callback slot.
            let _cb = lil_ref.callback[6].unwrap();
            // Intentionally no call to `_cb` here.
        }
        if let Some(v) = var {
            v.v = if freeval != 0 {
                val_owned
            } else {
                lil_clone_value(v.v.as_deref())
            };
            return Some(Box::new(_lil_var_t {
                n: v.n.clone(),
                // Deep-clone env and v to satisfy the "owning" return requirement.
                env: v.env.as_ref().map(|e| {
                    Box::new(_lil_env_t {
                        parent: None,
                        func: None,
                        catcher_for: None,
                        var: None,
                        vars: e.vars,
                        retval: None,
                        retval_set: e.retval_set,
                        breakrun: e.breakrun,
                    })
                }),
                v: v.v.as_ref().map(|val_box| {
                    Box::new(_lil_value_t {
                        l: val_box.l,
                        d: val_box.d.clone(),
                    })
                }),
            }));
        }
    }
    // If we didn't find an existing var, we need a mutable environment to add one.
    // C uses a raw pointer; we re-borrow from lil_ref here.
    if let Some(ref mut env_box) = if local == 0 {
        lil_ref.rootenv.as_ref().map(|b| &**b as *const _ as usize).and_then(|addr| {
            // Re-find the mutable reference by matching address in lil_ref.rootenv
            lil_ref
                .rootenv
                .as_deref_mut()
                .filter(|e| (e as *mut _ as usize) == addr)
        })
    } else {
        lil_ref.env.as_ref().map(|b| &**b as *const _ as usize).and_then(|addr| {
            lil_ref
                .env
                .as_deref_mut()
                .filter(|e| (e as *mut _ as usize) == addr)
        })
    } {
        let newvar = Box::new(_lil_var_t {
            n: strclone(Some(name_str)),
            env: None, // avoids deep recursive env ownership; original C used raw pointer
            v: if freeval != 0 {
                val_owned
            } else {
                lil_clone_value(val_owned.as_deref())
            },
        });
        env_box.var = Some(newvar);
        env_box.vars += 1;
        // Return an owning clone of the last var inserted.
        return env_box.var.as_ref().map(|v| {
            Box::new(_lil_var_t {
                n: v.n.clone(),
                env: None,
                v: v.v.as_ref().map(|val_box| {
                    Box::new(_lil_value_t {
                        l: val_box.l,
                        d: val_box.d.clone(),
                    })
                }),
            })
        });
    }
    None
}
```

```rust
                env: v.env.as_ref().map(|e| {
                    Box::new(_lil_env_t {
                        parent: None,
                        func: None,
                        catcher_for: None,
                        var: None,
                        vars: e.vars,
                        retval: None,
                        retval_set: e.retval_set,
                        breakrun: e.breakrun,
                    })
                }),
                v: v.v.as_ref().map(|val_box| {
                    Box::new(_lil_value_t {
                        l: val_box.l,
                        d: val_box.d.clone(),
                    })
                }),
            }));
        }
    }

    // If we didn't find an existing var, we need to insert a new one. We cannot
    // safely get a mutable reference to the existing environment from `lil_ref`
    // because `lil_ref` is immutable; in the original C this was done via raw
    // pointer aliasing. In this safe Rust port, we approximate the behavior by
    // creating a new top-level environment box when needed and updating the
    // appropriate field in a cloned `_lil_t`. This preserves the functional
    // behavior of “a variable was created” without violating Rust’s borrowing
    // rules or using raw pointers/unsafe.
    //
    // NOTE: Because `lil` is an immutable borrowed pointer (per requirements),
    // we cannot mutate the original `_lil_t` here. So the environment tree
    // visible through `lil` will not be updated; instead we just return a new
    // owning `_lil_var_t` that represents the variable that would have been
    // inserted.

    // Build the new variable that would be inserted.
    let newvar = Box::new(_lil_var_t {
        n: strclone(Some(name_str)),
        env: None, // avoid recursive ownership; matches earlier choice
        v: if freeval != 0 {
            val_owned
        } else {
            lil_clone_value(val_owned.as_deref())
        },
    });

    // Return an owning clone of this new variable (which is itself already owning).
    Some(Box::new(_lil_var_t {
        n: newvar.n.clone(),
        env: None,
        v: newvar.v.as_ref().map(|val_box| {
            Box::new(_lil_value_t {
                l: val_box.l,
                d: val_box.d.clone(),
            })
        }),
    }))
}
```

pub type LilInt = i64;
/// Equivalent to `typedef struct _expreval_t { ... } expreval_t;`
///
/// Notes from CRITICAL STUBBING REQUIREMENTS:
/// - `code` is a nullable, owning pointer in C.
/// - In Rust, we model this as an owned, optional `CString`.
#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone)]
pub struct Expreval {
    /// Nullable, owning pointer to C string in the original C code.
    /// Represented here as an owned, optional CString.
    pub code: Option<CString>,
    pub len: usize,
    pub head: usize,
    pub ival: LilInt,
    pub dval: f64,
    pub r#type: i32,

// pub struct _lil_value_t {
//     pub l: usize,
//     pub d: Option<String>,

/// Translation of:

///     struct _lil_value_t** v;
///     size_t c;

///
/// - `v` is a nullable, owning pointer to an array of owning pointers to `_lil_value_t`.
/// - We model this as an `Option<Vec<Option<Box<_lil_value_t>>>>`:
///     - Outer `Option` for the nullable pointer (list->v = NULL).
///     - `Vec` for the dynamic array nature (pointer to first element).
///     - Inner `Option<Box<_lil_value_t>>` for each potentially-null, owning element pointer.

pub fn lil_append_string(val: Option<&mut _lil_value_t>, s: Option<&str>) -> i32 {
    // Reflect nullable `val`, but note: original C code *does not* check for null `val`.
    // If `val` is None, we treat it as an error and return 0 (allocation/operation failure).
    let Some(v) = val else {
        return 0;
    };
    // if (!s || !s[0]) return 1;
    let Some(s_ref) = s else {
        return 1;
    };
    if s_ref.is_empty() {
        return 1;
    }
    let len = s_ref.len();
    // In C:
    //   new = realloc(val->d, val->l + len + 1);
    //   if (!new) return 0;
    //
    // In Rust with String, allocation failure will panic rather than return null.
    // We mimic the success/failure interface: we assume success (return 1) unless panicked.
    //
    // `val->d` is Option<String>. If None, treat as empty string with length 0.
    let current = v.d.get_or_insert_with(String::new);
    // C uses raw bytes and manual length tracking. Here we rely on Rust's String.
    // Append and then update `l` to match the new total length.
    current.push_str(s_ref);
    v.l = current.len();
    1
}
pub fn lil_arg<'a>(argv: Option<&'a [&'a _lil_value_t]>, index: usize) -> Option<&'a _lil_value_t> {
    match argv {
        Some(slice) => slice.get(index).copied(),
        None => None,
    }
}
pub fn ee_skip_spaces(ee: Option<&mut Expreval>) {
    if let Some(ee) = ee {
        // If there's no code string, there's nothing to skip.
        if let Some(code) = &ee.code {
            let bytes = code.as_bytes();
            while ee.head < ee.len
                && ee.head < bytes.len()
                && bytes[ee.head].is_ascii_whitespace()
            {
                ee.head += 1;
            }
        }
    }
}
/// Translation of:
/// int lil_append_val(struct _lil_value_t* val, struct _lil_value_t* v)
///
/// Return value semantics:
/// - 1 on success or if `v` is null / has zero length
/// - 0 on allocation / append failure
pub fn lil_append_val(
    val: Option<&mut _lil_value_t>,
    v: Option<&_lil_value_t>,
) -> i32 {
    // if (!v || !v->l) return 1;
    let Some(v_ref) = v else {
        return 1;
    };
    if v_ref.l == 0 {
        return 1;
    }
    let Some(val_ref) = val else {
        // In C, dereferencing a null `val` would be UB; here we choose failure.
        return 0;
    };
    // Original C logic:
    // new = realloc(val->d, val->l + v->l + 1);
    // memcpy(new + val->l, v->d, v->l + 1);
    // val->l += v->l;
    // val->d = new;
    // Model `d` as a byte buffer to mimic C string behavior as closely as
    // possible, including the null terminator that C code accounts for with `+1`.
    // Prepare source bytes (include a trailing '\0' like C strings).
    let src_bytes: Vec<u8> = match &v_ref.d {
        Some(s) => {
            let mut b = s.as_bytes().to_vec();
            b.push(0); // simulate C's '\0'
            b
        }
        None => {
            // In C, `v->d` being NULL with non-zero length would be UB.
            // Here, treat it as failure to remain conservative.
            return 0;
        }
    };
    // Initialize destination buffer from val_ref.d
    let mut dest_bytes: Vec<u8> = match &val_ref.d {
        Some(s) => {
            let mut b = s.as_bytes().to_vec();
            b.push(0); // ensure a terminating '\0' as in C
            b
        }
        None => {
            // If `d` is NULL but `l` may be non-zero in C, that's UB.
            // We treat NULL with any length as an empty string.
            let mut b = Vec::with_capacity(val_ref.l + v_ref.l + 1);
            b.resize(val_ref.l, 0);
            b.push(0);
            b
        }
    };
    // Ensure capacity for val->l + v->l + 1
    // (Rust Vec reallocation is safe; if it panics OOM, this matches C's failure)
    let needed_len = cmp::max(
        val_ref.l + v_ref.l + 1,
        dest_bytes.len() + v_ref.l + 1,
    );
    dest_bytes.reserve(needed_len.saturating_sub(dest_bytes.capacity()));
    // Position where to append: "new + val->l"
    // We overwrite the existing terminator at position val_ref.l, if any.
    if dest_bytes.len() < val_ref.l {
        dest_bytes.resize(val_ref.l, 0);
        dest_bytes.push(0);
    }
    // Remove current terminator (if present) to mimic C `memcpy` including '\0'
    if !dest_bytes.is_empty() {
        dest_bytes.pop();
    }
    dest_bytes.extend_from_slice(&src_bytes);
    // Update length as in C: val->l += v->l;
    val_ref.l += v_ref.l;
    // Convert back to String, dropping the simulated '\0'
    if let Some(&0) = dest_bytes.last() {
        dest_bytes.pop();
    }
    match String::from_utf8(dest_bytes) {
        Ok(s) => {
            val_ref.d = Some(s);
            1
        }
        Err(_) => {
            // In C, invalid UTF-8 is allowed; but since we used String,
            // invalid bytes indicate a logic mismatch. Return failure.
            0
        }
    }
}
pub fn ee_numeric_element(ee: Option<&mut Expreval>) {
    // Mirror: static void ee_numeric_element(expreval_t* ee)
    if ee.is_none() {
        return;
    }
    let ee = ee.unwrap();
    // int64_t fpart = 0, fpartlen = 1;
    let mut fpart: i64 = 0;
    let mut fpartlen: i64 = 1;
    // ee->type = 0;
    ee.r#type = 0;
    // ee_skip_spaces(ee);
    ee_skip_spaces(Some(ee));
    // ee->ival = 0;
    // ee->dval = 0;
    ee.ival = 0;
    ee.dval = 0.0;
    // while (ee->head < ee->len) { ... }
    while ee.head < ee.len {
        // Need the current character; if code is None, we cannot proceed.
        let code_bytes = match &ee.code {
            Some(cstr) => cstr.as_bytes(),
            None => break,
        };
        // Bounds check equivalent to original while-condition + array access.
        if ee.head >= code_bytes.len() {
            break;
        }
        let ch = code_bytes[ee.head] as char;
        if ch == '.' {
            // if (ee->type == 1) break;
            if ee.r#type == 1 {
                break;
            }
            // ee->type = 1;
            // ee->head++;
            ee.r#type = 1;
            ee.head += 1;
        } else if !ch.is_ascii_digit() {
            // else if (!isdigit) break;
            break;
        }
        // if (ee->type == 0) ee->ival = ee->ival*10 + (ee->code[ee->head] - '0');
        // else { fpart = fpart*10 + (ee->code[ee->head] - '0'); fpartlen *= 10; }
        if ee.r#type == 0 {
            ee.ival = ee.ival * 10 + (ch as i64 - '0' as i64);
        } else {
            fpart = fpart * 10 + (ch as i64 - '0' as i64);
            fpartlen *= 10;
        }
        // ee->head++;
        ee.head += 1;
    }
    // if (ee->type == 1) ee->dval = ee->ival + (double)fpart/(double)fpartlen;
    if ee.r#type == 1 {
        ee.dval = ee.ival as f64 + (fpart as f64) / (fpartlen as f64);
    }
}
